paragraphs: Friend, this is a heavy one. A husband feels jealous, and there's no witness and no proof either way (Numbers 5:13) (Numbers 5:14). That feeling can write a whole movie off one weird silence, and this law sends it somewhere else. He brings his wife to the priest, and she stands before the LORD (Numbers 5:15) (Numbers 5:16).

Here's the lesson. The matter goes before the LORD, not into the husband's own hands. Listen to how the text keeps coming back to that: she stands before the LORD (Numbers 5:16), the offering is waved before the LORD (Numbers 5:25), and the priest applies to her "this entire law" (Numbers 5:30). What was concealed is put in front of Him.

The text says what happens either way. If she has been unfaithful, the water brings bitter suffering (Numbers 5:27). If she is clean, "she will be unaffected and able to conceive children" (Numbers 5:28). So when your own heart starts spinning with doubt, friend, take it to the LORD first, before you take it anywhere else.
